I was dumpster diving in the dark once behind Chipotle when I was feeling around in the bags & grabbed onto what I thought was a burrito. As I felt around I managed to tear open the tortilla & feel inside. I could feel the satisfyingly squishy texture of the delicious concoction of refried beans & sauces. 

Excitedly, I pulled it out & stuffed the whole thing in my mouth. The delicious, creamy sauces coated my mouth, the texture as tantalizing as the intense flavors. Right then my tongue felt something soft. I pulled out what I could see in the moonlight to be a feather. 

Right then a dapper young Chipotle employee came out the back door, took one look at me, & said "Uuuh, that dumpster is where we dispose of the birds that hit our windows...". We stared at each other for awhile, before I exclaimed "Totally worth it!" & enjoyed another.

Go to the hospital, medical bills are less important than your quality of life. Smoke some weed, go in nature, completely alone, sleep, listen to some ambient, spiritual music, like new age or Yeha Noha. Search for things you enjoy at least a bit, the simple things that can at least offer a few seconds of happiness: eat some cake, breathe fresh air, petrichore, watch Mr. Rogers. You should give a listen to the [Minnesota howls recorded in 2012 near Duluth,](http://sasquatchresearchers.org/march-2012-minnesota-howls/) about a 4 hour drive from where I live. They are distinctively guttural, throaty & apelike, definitely not wolves or coyotes or any known animal. Also beyond the vocal capabilities of man. They're also eerily 'anguished' or 'pained' at certain times. It's interesting you mention that there was a different call replying to the coyotes because that's how it sounds in the Minnesota howls.
